reproduce.title: Test Right Alt remapping for AltGr
reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys development build on supported Windows
prerequisites: Use Norwegian or another layout where AltGr+2 produces @.
Enable Keyboard Manager and configure AltGr/RightAlt→regular Alt.
steps: With remapping off, press AltGr+2 and confirm the layout character.
Test ordinary Ctrl+Alt+2 and plain right-Alt shortcuts; record whether AltGr is distinguished.
reproduce.expected_result: Remapped AltGr acts as regular Alt, while ordinary Ctrl+Alt and other right-Alt shortcuts remain correct.

judgment.rationale: The report explains AltGr behavior on an international layout. Latest duplicate activity resolves in favor of #3641: #35987 is closed with a comment pointing here, while #3641 remains open. Ctrl+RightAlt representation is plausible but unconfirmed for the reporter's Norwegian keyboard.
evidence: Open Issue-Bug, Priority-1, Product-Keyboard Manager; no assignee.
Body reports Windows 10.0.18363.836/PowerToys 0.18.1, Norwegian layout, RightAlt/AltGr→Alt, but AltGr+2 still types @; screenshots are included.
On 2026-04-19 #3641 was discussed as duplicate of #35987, but #35987 is now closed and its latest maintainer comment says duplicate of #3641; #3641 remains open.
An April 2026 commenter says German hardware emits Left Ctrl+Right Alt for AltGr; this supports testing, not proof of Norwegian event stream.
judgment.recommended_action: Treat #3641 as canonical and reproduce AltGr→Alt on current code, checking whether paired Ctrl survives the remap.

title: [KBM] Mapping ALT GR to ALT doesn't work

fix_assessment.rationale: #35987 is closed as a duplicate of #3641, not a separate fix; no linked PR is recorded. A plausible input-normalization hypothesis remains to test.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize AltGr input before remapping Right Alt
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: some international layouts represent AltGr as Ctrl+RightAlt, so a RightAlt-only mapping leaves Ctrl active and the layout still generates AltGr characters. The original Norwegian event stream is unconfirmed.
plan: Reproduce AltGr+2 before/after RightAlt→Alt on current PowerToys with Norwegian or equivalent layout; record observed modifiers.
Trace whether Ctrl is physical, synthesized or layout-generated and how Keyboard Manager applies the RightAlt remap.
If paired AltGr is confirmed, normalize the pair at the remap boundary and test without changing ordinary Ctrl+Alt behavior.
verification: After remapping, AltGr+2 behaves as regular Alt rather than producing @, while the intended Ctrl+Alt sequence still yields the layout character.
Verify plain right-Alt shortcuts and left/right Ctrl/Alt key-up behavior remain correct.

confidence.rationale: Concrete report and a related German-layout comment support the hypothesis, but do not confirm the Norwegian keyboard's event stream.

issue_context.summary: On a Norwegian keyboard, mapping AltGr (detected as Right Alt) to regular Alt does not stop AltGr+2 from typing @.
known_information: Open Issue-Bug, Priority-1, Product-Keyboard Manager; no assignee.
Body reports Windows 10.0.18363.836/PowerToys 0.18.1 and includes mapping screenshots.
Reporter expects AltGr+2 to behave as regular Alt+2; it still produces @.
#35987 is closed and its latest comment points back to #3641, which remains open.
inferences: A paired Ctrl+RightAlt representation may survive remapping, but original layout events are unknown.
The current issue states identify #3641 as canonical despite contradictory earlier duplicate notes.
issue_context.analysis: The expected/actual behavior is concrete; maintainer-side layout reproduction is more useful than requesting generic logs. Keep the hypothesis yellow because the paired modifier evidence comes from another layout.
